title: Photographed Bengali Artisan Idol
positive: A photograph of a magnificent hand-crafted Bengali clay idol of the goddess Durga, sculpted and painted by traditional Kumartuli artisans, displayed alone and centered in a wide panoramic frame as a peaceful devotional portrait. The idol stands frontal and serene, filling the frame vertically from just above the tip of her ornate gold crown to her feet, the crown fully visible. The painted face is large, luminous and exceptionally beautiful, with a smooth golden skin tone, two matching elongated almond eyes outlined in black, both perfectly aligned and looking straight at the viewer with calm grace, and a small vertical third eye painted in the center of her forehead, distinct from the two natural eyes. Gently closed lips. She is dressed in a red silk sari with heavy gold zari work and adorned with opulent gold jewelry, crown, earrings, necklaces and armlets, with a few restrained diamond accents catching the light. A sculpted gold halo disc stands behind her head. Ten sculpted arms, five emerging from each shoulder region, fan outward evenly in a clean arc, each with a coherent elbow, wrist and fingers, each hand gripping one distinct object: trident, sword, discus, conch, bow, arrow, bell, axe, shield, coiled noose. A single realistically proportioned sculpted lion with a full mane sits at her feet, calm and noble, with two matching eyes. Black backdrop with wide dark empty space on both sides. Warm spotlight, 50mm lens, fine clay and paint texture, sharp focus on the face.
